_README: Hand-picked photographs, keyed by scientific name, valued by iNaturalist observation id. Photos are otherwise chosen by community votes, which reward a striking or curious picture rather than a legible one. Six of the eight best-voted Eastern Blue Groper shots are head-on portraits; five of eight Red Morwong; and the top-voted Australasian Snapper is a BLEACHED SKULL on a rock — a valid record, research grade, and no use whatever to someone trying to name a fish they just swam past. Prefer a side-on view of one whole living animal. Paste the observation id from the 'see the observation' link. Delete an entry to hand the choice back to the ranking. A fourth pattern shows up past rank 80: the animal held in a hand, in a plastic bag, or dead on the sand. Colours shift out of water and the context is wrong for a guide used in it.
_note_mola_alexandrini: The actual animal, in this bay, on 6 September 2026 — Michal's second frame, which is the near-side-on one: whole fish, tall dorsal and anal fins, the mottled flank, the clavus, and the bay's own sand and kelp behind it. His first frame is three-quarters on and his third is a portrait of the eye and beak; both are good pictures and neither is the one that helps you name it. Replaces the 2016 Manly record, which was the best available until this fish turned up and is still the second-best photograph of the species anywhere.
